name: nano-banana
works_with: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode
short: Makes slide decks and illustrations with Google's Nano Banana image models.
what: Plans a slide deck with you, then makes each slide as an image with Google's Gemini image models (Nano Banana). You review the slides in your browser, it redoes the ones you flag, and it packs everything into a PowerPoint file. It can also make figures and illustrations.
who: People who want their agent to make image-based slide decks or illustrations and are happy to pay for Gemini API use. The slides are images, so you can't edit the text in PowerPoint afterwards.
needs: A Google Gemini API key, set as `GOOGLE_API_KEY`. Google lists no free tier for these image models: roughly $0.07 to $0.24 per image
Python packages: `pip install pillow google-genai python-pptx python-dotenv`
A coding agent that supports skills

steps.title: Add the skills
steps.text: This installs all 16 EvoSkills, including nano-banana:

steps.title: Install the Python packages
steps.code: pip install pillow google-genai python-pptx python-dotenv

steps.title: Set your API key
steps.text: Put it in your environment rather than pasting it into chat, so it doesn't end up in transcripts.

steps.title: Fix the model names (important)
steps.text: As of 3 Oct 2026, the skill's scripts only accept three model names, and Google's deprecations page lists all three as shut down (two on 25 June 2026, one on 2 October 2026). Until the skill is updated, edit `SUPPORTED_MODELS` and `DEFAULT_MODEL` in `scripts/generate_ppt.py` and `scripts/edit_slide.py` to the replacement names Google gives: `gemini-3-pro-image` or `gemini-3.1-flash-image`. We haven't tested this fix with a live key.

try.label: Suggested
try.text:
Make me a 5-slide presentation on <your topic> in the Lineal Color style.

The skill asks about audience, length and language before it generates anything.

watch: Check the skill's GitHub page for an update to the model names before you start.
Every image is a paid API call. Regenerating the deck redoes every slide, and each edit is another call. A 12-slide deck on the Pro model is roughly $1.60 before edits.
It runs a small local web server (port 8080 by default) for reviewing slides. Stop it with `package_pptx.py --kill-server` when you're done.
